title: Hal Sets Up a Pen
lines: Hal has ten hens but not a pen.
"The hens are in the mud," said Dad.
Hal gets logs. Dad cuts the logs.
Hal digs a pit and sets the logs in.
But a log tips, and a hen runs!
Hal digs the pit and pats mud on it.
The log is set. Hal gets the hen.
"Look, Dad! Ten hens in the pen," said Hal.

questions.ask: Why did Hal need a pen for the hens?
questions.listenFor: Because the hens kept getting in the mud. Line two says it. Let your child reread it rather than being told.

questions.ask: What went wrong while Hal was setting the logs?
questions.listenFor: A log tipped over and a hen got out. Line five says it. If they only say "a hen got out," ask what made that happen.

questions.ask: What else could Hal do to keep the hens out of the mud? Tell me why that would work.
questions.listenFor: There is no wrong answer. You are listening for a reason that shows they understood the problem.
